description.text: A collection of static configuration properties that govern the execution of the discrete-event reinforcement learning simulation for CPRO camera assembly lines.
List of modeling approaches used for the model.
Maximum number of training episodes for the PPO reinforcement learning agent. Early termination applies if convergence is detected before this limit.

A collection of process node definitions used to construct the ProcessKnowledgeGraph for reinforcement learning. Each child collection represents a product model, and its sub-collections represent individual process nodes with feature values used as GNN input.

A collection of process node definitions for MODEL_A (VD7) used as graph nodes in the ProcessKnowledgeGraph. Each child collection represents an individual process node with its rated power consumption value.
Process node for VD7_10 firmware input step. Rated power is allocated from MODULE group compressor consumption proportional to CycleTimeSec ratio (25s / 415s = 6.02%).

Cycle time of process VD7_10_FW in seconds. Time required for one unit to complete IP F/W input via USB Jig Board (NO44-FW_JIG). Based on 6 jig boards assigned to the firmware input line with 2 workers.

Defect rate of process VD7_10_FW. No step-specific defect rate has been recorded in the reference data. A minimum defect rate of 0.001 (0.1%) is applied based on the assumption that marginal process variation is inherent in any manufacturing step. The overall assembly line defect rate entering the inspection process is defined as 0.3% or below.
F/W input process. Equipment: F/W JIG (no direct power) + Computer (0.15kW × 6) + Monitor (0.0155kW × 6) allocated equally across 4 MODULE_FW processes by CT ratio 25%.

Process 10-1 — IP F/W verification. Firmware data loaded in process 10 is verified against product and buyer specification using OEM specification document. No additional input materials consumed at this step. Equipment: input program — criterion: DATA input confirmed (computer bug managemen). Cautiton: firmware must match product and buyer specification; observe input sequence order.
Cycle time of process VD7_10-1_FW in seconds. Time required for one unit to complete IP F/W verification using the input program.

Defect rate of process VD7_10_1_FW. No step-specific defect rate has been recorded in the reference data. A minimum defect rate of 0.001 (0.1%) is applied based on the assumption that marginal process variation is inherent in any manufacturing step. The overall assembly line defect rate entering the inspection process is defined as 0.3% or below.
F/W input process. Equipment: F/W JIG (no direct power) + Computer (0.15kW × 6) + Monitor (0.0155kW × 6) allocated equally across 4 MODULE_FW processes by CT ratio 25%.

Process 10-2 — IP F/W secondary confirmation. Confirms 100% completion of firmware input performed in process 10 and 10-1. Firmware compliance with product and buyer specification is re-confirmed using OEM specification document. No additional input materials consumed at this step. Equipment: input program — criterion: DATA input confirmed (computer bug management). Caution: confirm full input completion before proceeding; observe input sequence order.
Cycle time of process VD7_10-2_FW in seconds. Time required for one unit to complete IP F/W verification using the input program.

Defect rate of process VD7_10-2_FW. No step-specific defect rate has been recorded in the reference data. A minimum defect rate of 0.001 (0.1%) is applied as the process-level default until step-specific measurement data becomes available.
F/W secondary confirmation. Same equipment allocation as VD7_10 by CT ratio 25%.

Process 10-3 — MAC address and MODEL name input. Unique MAC address (assigned per unit) and model name (NAF3-OLAH4) are programmed into the device using the input program. MAC address must not be duplicated across units; model name input must be verified via cpro show command. No additional input materials consumed at this step. Revision 1.6 issued 2021-09-23: MAC label attachment position changed. Output of this step proceeds to process 30 (VD7_30_FOCUS).
Cycle time of process VD7_10-2_FW in seconds. Time required for one unit to complete IP F/W verification using the input program.
MAC/model name programming. Same equipment allocation as VD7_10 by CT ratio 25%.

Defect rate of process VD7_10-2_FW. No step-specific defect rate has been recorded in the reference data. A minimum defect rate of 0.001 (0.1%) is applied as the process-level default until step-specific measurement data becomes available.

Process 20 — SENSOR BOARD assembly. M12 CNC-machined lens holder (20502140), TDN actuator (50100541, NX-X-05B25C 21/145), M12 lens (10800565), lens fix nut (20901092), and screw (30300592) are assembled onto the sensor board sub-assembly. 5 input materials consumed per unit. Equipment: electric driver — torque spec 0.8~1.2 kgf·cm. Revision 1.4 issued 2021-04-07: lens holder post-processing changed to CNC machining (ECO514).

Cycle time of process VD7_20_SENSOR in seconds. Time required for one unit to complete SENSOR BOARD assembly including lens holder mounting, TDN actuator installation, and screw fastening with torque confirmation.

Defect rate of process VD7_20_SENSOR. No step-specific defect rate has been recorded in the reference data. A minimum defect rate of 0.001 (0.1%) is applied based on the assumption that marginal process variation is inherent in any manufacturing step. The overall assembly line defect rate entering the inspection process is defined as 0.3% or below.
Sensor board assembly. Compressor (CKV300 22kW + HS100E 75kW) allocated by CT ratio 34.29% within MODULE group.

Process 20-1 — SENSOR BOARD integration onto main board PCB (03203124, SMT MBR5600_IP-R1). The completed sensor board sub-assembly from process 20 is mounted onto the main board PCB using sponge insulation seat (21200743, qty 1) and cross-head screws (30300125, qty 2). Torque spec: 1.5~2 kgf·cm. TDN orientation, absence of foreign matter, and connector integrity must be confirmed visually. Upon completion, sub-assemblies are transferred to the next line via CART (transfer qty: 80 units per batch).
Sensor board sub-assembly. Compressor allocated by CT ratio 33.97% within MODULE group.

Cycle time of process VD7_20-1_SENSOR in seconds. Time required for one unit to complete SENSOR BOARD integration onto main board PCB including insulation seat placement, screw fastening with torque confirmation, and visual inspection of TDN orientation and connector integrity.

Defect rate of process VD7_20_1_SENSOR. No step-specific defect rate has been recorded in the reference data. A minimum defect rate of 0.001 (0.1%) is applied based on the assumption that marginal process variation is inherent in any manufacturing step. The overall assembly line defect rate entering the inspection process is defined as 0.3% or below.

Process 30 — FOCUS SETTING. Optical focus is adjusted on the sensor board sub-assembly received from process 10-3 (MAC/MODEL name input). Focus quality is assessed visually using dome cover as reference fixture. Lens protrusion confirmed at 15 mm using vernier caliper. Absence of foreign matter and connector integrity confirmed visually before step completion. No input materials consumed at this step.
Focus adjustment. Compressor allocated by CT ratio 31.75% within MODULE group. UV curer (0.4kW) excluded (NVD only).

Defect rate of process VD7_30_FOCUS. No step-specific defect rate has been recorded in the reference data. A minimum defect rate of 0.001 (0.1%) is applied based on the assumption that marginal process variation is inherent in any manufacturing step. The overall assembly line defect rate entering the inspection process is defined as 0.3% or below.

Cycle time of process VD7_30_FOCUS in seconds. Time required for one unit to complete focus adjustment including dome cover inspection, vernier caliper measurement of lens protrusion at 15 mm, and visual confirmation of foreign matter absence and connector integrity.

Process 40 — GIMBAL ASS'Y. Gimbal front housing (20501683), IR PCB (03902715, SMT VD7_H2IR-R1), IR rubber (21200734), and screws (30300165, qty 3) are assembled into a gimbal sub-assembly. IR rubber must be confirmed intact without tearing or damage. IR rubber orientation and seating onto gimbal front confirmed visually against reference photograph. Torque spec: 1.5~2 kgf·cm. Revision 1.1 issued 2020-07-28: LED bracket changed (ECO467).
Gimbal assembly. Electric drivers + compressor allocated by CT ratio 6.87% within SEMI group.

Cycle time of process VD7_40_GIMBAL in seconds. Time required for one unit to complete gimbal front housing assembly including IR PCB mounting, IR rubber seating with orientation confirmation, and screw fastening with torque confirmation.

Defect rate of process VD7_40_GIMBAL. No step-specific defect rate has been recorded in the reference data. A minimum defect rate of 0.001 (0.1%) is applied based on the assumption that marginal process variation is inherent in any manufacturing step. The overall assembly line defect rate entering the inspection process is defined as 0.3% or below.

Process 40-1 — GIMBAL ASS'Y integration. JOIN step merging gimbal sub-assembly (VD7_40_GIMBAL) and sensor board sub-assembly (VD7_20-1_SENSOR). Gimbal module bracket (20901361) and tilt bracket (20900508) are mounted and fastened using tapping screws (30300433, qty 3). IR harness direction confirmed against reference photograph. IR rubber and lens centre alignment confirmed visually. Connector integrity confirmed visually. Torque spec: 1.5~2 kgf·cm. Sub-assemblies transferred to next line via CART (transfer qty: 80 units per batch).
Gimbal sub-assembly JOIN. Electric drivers + compressor allocated by CT ratio 6.57% within SEMI group.

Defect rate of process VD7_40-1_GIMBAL. No step-specific defect rate has been recorded in the reference data. A minimum defect rate of 0.001 (0.1%) is applied based on the assumption that marginal process variation is inherent in any manufacturing step. The overall assembly line defect rate entering the inspection process is defined as 0.3% or below.

Cycle time of process VD7_40-1_GIMBAL in seconds. Time required for one unit to complete gimbal module bracket and tilt bracket mounting including IR harness direction confirmation, lens and IR rubber centre alignment verification, connector integrity check, and screw fastening with torque confirmation.

Process 50 — BOTTOM ASSY. Bottom case (20502127), cable rubber grommet (21201260), waterproof cable assembly RJ45+DCJ (20200832), and cable tie (30400735) are assembled into the bottom case sub-assembly. Cable rubber and cable tie routing must be confirmed. Independent process starting upon SMT_COMPLETE.
Bottom case assembly. Electric drivers + compressor allocated by CT ratio 19.10% within SEMI group.

Cycle time of process VD7_50_BOTTOM in seconds. Time required for one unit to complete bottom case assembly including cable rubber grommet installation, waterproof cable routing, and cable tie securing.

Defect rate of process VD7_50_BOTTOM. Based on reference data indicating overall assembly line defect rate of 0.3% or below. A minimum defect rate of 0.001 (0.1%) is applied as the process-level default.

Process 50-1 — BOTTOM ASSY integration. JOIN step merging VD7_50_BOTTOM (bottom case sub-assembly) and VD7_30_FOCUS (focus-adjusted sub-assembly). Thermal pad (21200538) is placed on main board PCB surface. Main board PCB is fastened onto bottom case using cross-head screws (30300124, qty 3). Micro coaxial wire harness (21600655) is connected between sensor PCB and main board PCB. Connector seating, cable routing, and thermal pad positioning confirmed visually before step completion.
Bottom case sub-assembly JOIN. Electric drivers + compressor allocated by CT ratio 18.81% within SEMI group.

Defect rate of process VD7_50_1_BOTTOM. Based on reference data indicating overall assembly line defect rate of 0.3% or below. A minimum defect rate of 0.001 (0.1%) is applied as the process-level default.

Cycle time of process VD7_50-1_BOTTOM in seconds. Time required for one unit to complete thermal pad placement, main board PCB fastening with screw torque confirmation, and micro coaxial wire harness connection with connector seating verification.

Process 50-2 — BOTTOM ASSY completion. Gimbal support bracket (20501665) with sponge pad (21201264) and gimbal rotation limits bracket (20901652) are mounted onto the integrated bottom case sub-assembly from process 50-1 using cross-head screws (30300124, qty 4). Bracket seating position and rotation limits bracket orientation confirmed visually against reference photograph. Sub-assemblies transferred to the next line via CART (transfer qty: 80 units per batch).
Bottom case final assembly. Electric drivers + compressor allocated by CT ratio 18.81% within SEMI group.

Cycle time of process VD7_50-2_BOTTOM in seconds. Time required for one unit to complete gimbal support bracket and sponge pad placement, rotation limits bracket installation with orientation confirmation, and screw fastening with torque confirmation.

Defect rate of process VD7_50_2_BOTTOM. Based on reference data indicating overall assembly line defect rate of 0.3% or below. A minimum defect rate of 0.001 (0.1%) is applied as the process-level default.

Process 60 — GIMBAL + BOTTOM ASS'Y. JOIN step merging VD7_40-1_GIMBAL (gimbal integration sub-assembly) and VD7_50-2_BOTTOM (bottom case completed sub-assembly). Cross-head screws (30300124, qty 2) fasten the gimbal and bottom case assemblies together. MCX cable must be connected without damage or incomplete insertion. Gimbal assembly orientation confirmed against reference photograph. Connector integrity confirmed visually. Torque spec: 1.5~2 kgf·cm. Caution: MCX cable connector and cable damage must be avoided during fastening; screw thread wear and idle fastening must be prevented. Sub-assemblies transferred via CART (transfer qty: 80 units per batch).
Combined assembly JOIN. Electric drivers + compressor allocated by CT ratio 36.55% within SET group.

Defect rate of process VD7_60_COMB. Based on reference data indicating overall assembly line defect rate of 0.3% or below. A minimum defect rate of 0.001 (0.1%) is applied as the process-level default.

Cycle time of process VD7_60_COMB in seconds. Time required for one unit to complete gimbal and bottom case mechanical fastening including MCX cable connection verification, gimbal orientation confirmation, connector integrity check, and screw fastening with torque confirmation.

Process 70 — Camera Test inspection stage 1. First of three sequential inspection steps performed on the combined assembly (VD7_60_COMB output). Functional and visual inspection of the assembled camera module conducted by inspection-dedicated sub-group within WORKER_SET. No input materials consumed at this step. Defect rate: 0.003. Non-conforming units diverted to RMA repair process.
Cycle time of process VD7_70_INSP in seconds. Time required for one unit to complete the first stage of camera functional and visual inspection.
Inspection process. Computer (0.15kW) + Monitor + PoE allocated by CT ratio 20.30% within SET group.

Defect rate of process VD7_70_INSP. Based on reference data indicating overall assembly line defect rate of 0.3% or below. A minimum defect rate of 0.001 (0.1%) is applied as the process-level default.

Process 70-1 — Camera Test inspection stage 2. Second of three sequential inspection steps performed on the output of process 70. Functional and visual inspection continues by inspection-dedicated sub-group within WORKER_SET. No input materials consumed at this step. Defect rate: 0.003. Non-conforming units diverted to RMA repair process.

Defect rate of process VD7_70-1_INSP. Based on reference data indicating overall assembly line defect rate of 0.3% or below. A minimum defect rate of 0.001 (0.1%) is applied as the process-level default.
Cycle time of process VD7_70-1_INSP in seconds. Time required for one unit to complete the second stage of camera functional and visual inspection.
Inspection sub-process. Computer + Monitor + PoE allocated by CT ratio 20.30% within SET group.

Process 70-2 — Camera Test inspection stage 3. Third and final inspection step performed on the output of process 70-1. Functional and visual inspection completed by inspection-dedicated sub-group within WORKER_SET. No input materials consumed at this step. Defect rate: 0.003. Non-conforming units diverted to RMA repair process. Output of this step proceeds to VD7_90_SET (SET assembly JOIN with upper housing sub-assembly).
Inspection final check. Computer + Monitor + PoE allocated by CT ratio 20.30% within SET group.

Defect rate of process VD7_70-2_INSP. Based on reference data indicating overall assembly line defect rate of 0.3% or below. A minimum defect rate of 0.001 (0.1%) is applied as the process-level default.

Cycle time of process VD7_70-2_INSP in seconds. Time required for one unit to complete the third and final stage of camera functional and visual inspection before proceeding to SET assembly JOIN process.

Process 80 — UPPER ASS'Y. Independent process starting upon SMT_COMPLETE. Adhesive vent (21200533) attached to upper case (20501148). Dome cover (20901858), bubble gasket (21200496), and dome stopper (21100701) assembled into upper case. Upper case fastened using machine screws (30300540, qty 4). Vent attachment confirmed free of tearing and incomplete bonding. Bubble gasket orientation confirmed against reference photograph. Absence of foreign matter confirmed visually. Torque spec: 2~3 kgf·cm. Sub-assemblies transferred via CART (transfer qty: 80 units per batch). Revision history: ECO438 (Rev1.1, 2020-02-03) upper case press changed; ECO656 (Rev1.8, 2023-05-24) bubble changed; ECO754 (Rev1.9, 2024-10-25) bubble gasket and upper case updated.
Upper housing assembly. Electric drivers + compressor allocated by CT ratio 14.93% within SEMI group.

Cycle time of process VD7_80_UPPER in seconds. Time required for one unit to complete adhesive vent attachment, dome cover and bubble gasket orientation confirmation, dome stopper installation, and upper case screw fastening with torque confirmation.

Defect rate of process VD7_80_UPPER. Probability of a non-conforming unit occurring during upper housing sub-assembly, including vent attachment failure, gasket misorientation, or foreign matter contamination.

Process 80-1 — UPPER ASS'Y completion. Main gasket (21200511) is seated into the upper case groove and confirmed free of displacement. Upper case and bottom case housing assemblies are fastened together using Torx screws (30301017, qty 3). Gasket seating confirmed without displacement from case groove before fastening. Absence of foreign matter confirmed visually. Upper case surface scratching must be prevented during screw fastening. Torque spec: 2~3 kgf·cm. Sub-assemblies transferred via CART (transfer qty: 80 units per batch).

Defect rate of process VD7_80-1_UPPER. Probability of a non-conforming unit occurring during upper housing closure, including gasket displacement, incomplete housing closure, or surface damage during Torx screw fastening.
Upper housing sub-assembly. Electric drivers + compressor allocated by CT ratio 14.93% within SEMI group.

Cycle time of process VD7_80-1_UPPER in seconds. Time required for one unit to complete main gasket seating confirmation, upper and lower housing closure, and Torx screw fastening with torque confirmation.

Process 90 — SET ASS'Y. JOIN step merging VD7_70-2_INSP (inspection completed camera sub-assembly) and VD7_80-1_UPPER (upper housing completed sub-assembly). IR sponge (21200901) cleaned with methyl alcohol and assembled onto IR PCB surface. Dome cover protective film (21201365) attached to outer dome cover surface per ECO630 (Rev1.7, 2023-01-02). Absence of foreign matter and housing surface scratches confirmed visually. IR sponge cleaning effectiveness confirmed before assembly. Torque spec: 4~5 kgf·cm. Sub-assemblies transferred via CART (transfer qty: 80 units per batch).

Cycle time of process VD7_90_SET in seconds. Time required for one unit to complete IR sponge alcohol cleaning and installation, dome cover protective film attachment, and visual confirmation of foreign matter absence and housing surface integrity.

Defect rate of process VD7_90_SET. Probability of a non-conforming unit occurring during final SET assembly, including IR sponge contamination after cleaning, protective film misalignment, or housing surface scratching during closure.
SET assembly JOIN. Electric drivers + compressor allocated by CT ratio 2.54% within SET group.

Process 100 — AGING. Fully assembled camera units received from VD7_90_SET are subjected to an aging test to identify early-stage failures under operating conditions. No input materials consumed at this step. Units exhibiting anomalous behaviour during aging are diverted for inspection or repair before proceeding to packaging.
Cycle time of process VD7_100_AGING in seconds. Duration for which each assembled camera unit is operated under aging test conditions to detect latent defects before packaging.
Aging test process. Equipment: Computer (0.15kW × 9) + Monitor + PoE + Aging Test chamber (estimated 10kW for 9 units). Sole process in AGING group.
Defect rate of process VD7_100_AGING. Probability of a unit being identified as non-conforming during aging test due to latent assembly defects or component failure under operating conditions.

Process 110 — 포장 (accessory packaging). Mounting nuts (20900925, qty 2), mounting bolts (21000790, qty 2), L-wrench Torx T20 (21000072, qty 1), tapping screw (30300614, qty 1), antistatic bags (30500003, 30500004, qty 1 each), and RJ45 waterproof cap (21201287, qty 1) are prepared and packaged as accessories. Accessory completeness confirmed by visual inspection before proceeding to unit boxing. Revision history: ECO550 (Rev1.5, 2021-08-27): RJ45 cable waterproof cap added.

Cycle time of process VD7_110_PACK in seconds. Time required for one unit to complete accessory preparation and packaging including completeness confirmation of all seven accessory items by visual inspection.
Defect rate of process VD7_110_PACK. Probability of a non-conforming unit occurring due to missing or incorrect accessory items during the accessory packaging step.
Packaging. Compressor CKV300 (22kW) + HS100E (75kW) + vacuum packer (1.5kW) allocated by CT ratio 25.33% within PACK group.

Process 110-1 — 포장(박스) (unit box packaging). Camera unit and accessories placed into unit box (30200916) with PE foam bottom insert (21400282) and silica gel desiccant (30400105). Box and PE foam moulding defects confirmed absent by visual inspection. Accessory completeness confirmed before box closure. Quantity per unit: 1 box.
Packaging inner box. Same PACK group equipment allocated by CT ratio 25.33%.

Cycle time of process VD7_110-1_PACK in seconds. Time required for one unit to complete PE foam bottom placement, camera unit boxing, silica gel insertion, and visual confirmation of box and foam moulding quality.
Defect rate of process VD7_110-1_PACK. Probability of a non-conforming unit occurring due to foam moulding defects, missing silica gel, or incorrect camera placement during unit box packaging.

Process 110-2 — 포장(라벨부착) (label attachment). PE foam top insert (21400283) placed over camera unit inside unit box. Product label attached to unit box surface. Label print specification and serial number confirmed free of duplication by visual inspection. PE foam top moulding defects confirmed absent. Performed by WORKER_PACK_LABEL (2 persons).

Defect rate of process VD7_110-2_PACK. Probability of a non-conforming unit occurring due to label print specification mismatch, serial number duplication, or PE foam top moulding defects during label attachment.
Packaging inner box. Same PACK group equipment allocated by CT ratio 25.33%.

Cycle time of process VD7_110-2_PACK in seconds. Time required for one unit to complete PE foam top insert placement, product label attachment, and visual confirmation of label print specification and serial number uniqueness.

Process 110-3 — 포장(카톤박스) (carton box packaging). Mount template (30600066), CD manual (30401009), and carton box (30201152, qty 0.125, 1 carton per 8 units) complete the final packaging stage. Packaging material completeness confirmed by visual inspection. Label specification and attachment position confirmed before carton closure. This is the final process step of the MODEL_A VD7 assembly and packaging sequence.

Cycle time of process VD7_110-3_PACK in seconds. Time required for one unit to complete mount template and CD manual insertion, carton box closure, and visual confirmation of packaging material completeness and label specification compliance.

Defect rate of process VD7_110-3_PACK. Probability of a non-conforming unit occurring due to missing packaging materials, incorrect label attachment position, or carton box damage during final carton packaging.
Packaging outer box. PACK group equipment allocated by CT ratio 24.67%. Label printer excluded.

A collection of process node definitions for MODEL_B (BT5) used as graph nodes in the ProcessKnowledgeGraph. Each child collection represents an individual process node with its rated power consumption value.
Curing time required after adhesive application in BT5_42 bonding process. The assembled unit must remain stationary for this duration before proceeding to the next process.

A collection of process node definitions for MODEL_C (NVD) used as graph nodes in the ProcessKnowledgeGraph. Each child collection represents an individual process node with its rated power consumption value.

Process 20 — F/W Input with MAC and Model Setting. Firmware data is loaded into the SMT main board (03903388, NVD1_CV25M-1, qty 1) via USB Jig Board, and a unique MAC address and model name are programmed. Jig pin must be connected with power in OFF state before initiating data transfer. Equipment: NO44-FW_JIG and dedicated input program. Independent process triggered upon SMT_COMPLETE.

Process 21 — F/W Input. Continuation of firmware loading on the same SMT main board, performed sequentially after process 20. No additional input materials consumed at this step. Firmware compliance with product and buyer specification must be confirmed against OEM specification document. Input sequence order must be observed.

Process 22 — F/W Input. Final firmware loading and verification stage of the firmware input sequence. No additional input materials consumed at this step. 100% completion of firmware input is confirmed before the assembly advances to the next step.

Process 23 — F/W Input with MAC Label Attachment. Final step of the firmware input group. The MAC label (30101438, qty 1) carrying the assigned MAC address is attached to the SMT main board. Label print specification and serial number uniqueness must be confirmed before the sub-assembly is transferred to the front assembly line.

Process 30 — MODULE SUB ASSY. M12 lens (10800723, qty 1) is mounted onto the SMT main board (03203315, NVD1_5600-R1, qty 1) and fastened using cross-head black-plated screws (30300062, qty 2). Lens orientation and seating must be confirmed against reference photograph. Independent process triggered upon SMT_COMPLETE.

Focus adjustment process group for MODEL_C NVD1-75L-R(R1)/NVD1_5600(CV25S55M)/WH/N (CPRO향, NO LOGO). Contains one step: FOCUS SETTING with UV BOND (40). Optical focus is adjusted on the module sub-assembly received from process 30 and the lens position is fixed using ultraviolet-cured adhesive. Worker group: WORKER_SENSOR_FOCUS (3 persons). Equipment: NO30-UV_CURE (UV curing unit, OPAS Xlite 400P). Cycle time: 100 s. No additional input materials consumed. Revision 1.0 issued 2025-07-28.

Process 50 — FRONT ASSY. DC FRONT CASE (20502501, qty 1), Adhesive Vent — MIC (21201169, qty 1), LENS WINDOW gasket (21201481, qty 1), LED WINDOW gasket (21201486, qty 1), BODY gasket (21201482, qty 1), GLASS IR LED WINDOW (20400166, qty 1), and GLASS LENS WINDOW (20400165, qty 1) are assembled into the front case sub-assembly. Adhesive Vent must be confirmed free of damage. Each gasket must be confirmed correctly seated within the front case. WINDOW components must be installed with the protruding section oriented toward the outer surface. Independent process beginning upon SMT_COMPLETE.

Process 51 — FRONT ASSY (LED heat sink and POE/H2IR PCB). Machined LED HEAT SINK (21001371, qty 1), HEAT SINK THERMAL PAD (21201488, qty 1), and LED HEAT SINK adhesive double-sided tape (21201487, qty 1) are stacked on the front sub-assembly. Pressed WINDOW BRACKET (21101585, qty 1) is fastened with M2.5×5.0 machine screws (30300468, qty 4). The POE & H2IR SMT board (03903391, NVD1-POE&H2IR-R1, qty 1) is mounted onto the bracket and fastened with M2.0×4.0 cross-head screws (30300125, qty 2). Thermal pad and adhesive tape orientation must be confirmed visually before the PCB is installed.

Process 52 — FRONT ASSY (JOIN with focused module). JOIN step merging NVD_40_FOCUS (focused module sub-assembly) and NVD_51_FRONT (front housing with LED heat sink and POE/H2IR PCB). MOL5P-50 cable harness (21600574, qty 1) and TMT4P-50 cable harness (21600323, qty 1) are connected between the boards through machined SPACE BAR (21000172, qty 4) which provides the standoff distance. Connector seating and cable routing confirmed visually before transfer.

Process 53 — FRONT ASSY (JOIN with FW-input PCB). JOIN step merging NVD_23_FW (FW-input completed PCB sub-assembly) and NVD_52_FRONT (front sub-assembly with internal cables). M2.0×4.0 cross-head screws (30300125, qty 4) fasten the firmware-loaded PCB onto the front sub-assembly. PCB orientation, screw torque, and connector integrity confirmed visually before transfer. Sub-assemblies transferred to next line via CART (transfer qty: 80 units per batch).

Process 60 — REAR CASE ASSY. DC REAR CASE (20502502, qty 1) is prepared and SIDE COVER gasket (21201483, qty 1) and CABLE RUBBER (21201484, qty 1) are seated. M3.0×14.0 SUS flat-head screws (30300999, qty 4) are pre-installed on the rear case for subsequent fastening. Gasket and rubber seating must be confirmed without displacement before the next step. Independent process beginning upon SMT_COMPLETE.

Process 61 — REAR CASE ASSY (cable harness routing). The waterproof cable assembly RJ45+DCJ (20200899, qty 1) is routed through the rear case together with the O-ring terminal (20200819, qty 1) and pressed CABLE BRACKET-ST17 (21101550, qty 1). The bracket is fastened using M2.5×6 SUS screws (30301095, qty 3) and a single M2×4 black FH screw (30300303, qty 1). The cable bundle is secured by a cable tie (30402020, qty 1) and a wire harness core sleeve (21800016, qty 1) is applied. Cable routing direction and connector integrity confirmed visually. Sub-assemblies transferred via CART (transfer qty: 80 units per batch).

Process 70 — GIMBAL ASSY. JOIN step merging NVD_53_FRONT (front housing completed sub-assembly with FW-input PCB) and NVD_61_REAR (rear case completed sub-assembly with cable harness). The heater THERMAL PAD-SF1 (21201322, qty 1) is placed at the heater contact interface during convergence to ensure thermal coupling between the heater PCB and housing. Connector seating and pad positioning confirmed visually before fastening. This step is the gimbal-stage convergence point in the assembly flow.

Process 80 — SET ASSY (bottom housing). DC BOTTOM CASE (20502535, qty 1), CONDUIT CAP (21201310, qty 1), and BOTTOM GASKETs (21201497, qty 3) are assembled to form the bottom housing sub-assembly. Gasket seating and cap orientation confirmed visually before mounting. Independent process beginning upon SMT_COMPLETE.

Process 81 — SET ASSY (JOIN with gimbal-completed body). JOIN step merging NVD_70_GIMBAL (gimbal-completed camera body) and NVD_80_SET (bottom housing sub-assembly). DC TOP COVER (20502534, qty 1) and a Set Socket M4.0×8.0 SUS screw (30300965, qty 1) are added to fasten the top cover to the joined body. Cover orientation and connector integrity confirmed visually.

Process 82 — SET ASSY (label attachment). MAC label (30101438, qty 1) is attached to the assembled housing exterior. Label print specification and serial number uniqueness confirmed by visual inspection before the unit advances to the final SET stage.

Process 83 — SET ASSY (final). Final SET assembly stage completing the assembled camera unit prior to camera test inspection. Cycle time and detailed work content pending final standardisation; placeholder cycle time 0 s applied.

Process 90 — Camera Test inspection stage 1. First of three sequential inspection steps performed on the SET-completed camera unit. Functional and visual inspection conducted by an inspection-dedicated sub-group within WORKER_SET. No input materials consumed at this step. Non-conforming units diverted to RMA repair process.

Process 91 — Camera Test inspection stage 2. Second of three sequential inspection steps performed on the output of process 90. Functional and visual inspection continues. No input materials consumed at this step. Non-conforming units diverted to RMA repair process.

Process 92 — Camera Test inspection stage 3. Third and final inspection step performed on the output of process 91. Functional and visual inspection completed. No input materials consumed at this step. Output of this step proceeds to NVD_100_SIDE.

Process 100 — SIDE COVER 조립 (side cover assembly). Adhesive Vent — MIC (21201169, qty 1) is bonded to the DC SIDE COVER (20502503, qty 1). The side cover is fastened to the camera body using M3.0×8.0 SUS Torx-10 screws (30301034, qty 2) and M2×4 black FH screws (30300303, qty 2). WINDOW protection film (21201212, qty 1) and LED WINDOW protection film (21201490, qty 1) are applied. DESI-TOP 2g desiccant (30402885, qty 1) and DESIPAK STICKER (30101499, qty 1) are placed inside before closure. Vent attachment, screw torque, and film placement confirmed visually before transfer.

Process 110 — Aging Test. Fully assembled camera units received from NVD_100_SIDE are operated for a defined duration under aging test conditions to detect early-stage failure mechanisms. No input materials consumed at this step. Units exhibiting anomalous behaviour during aging are diverted for inspection or repair before proceeding to packaging. Sub-assemblies transferred via CART (transfer qty: 80 units per batch).

Process 120 — 포장 (accessory packaging). Field installation accessories are prepared and packaged alongside the finished camera unit. Items included: DESI-TOP 2g VIETNAM vacuum-packed desiccant (30402886, qty 1), anchor T/S-1 PHL+ D3×35 with calblock 3EA set (30301127, qty 1), L-WRENCH HEX2.0 (30401685, qty 1), L-WRENCH T10 TORX (21000140, qty 1), RJ45 CABLE WATER PROOF CAP (21201287, qty 1), and antistatic bag (30500003, qty 1). Accessory completeness confirmed by visual inspection before proceeding to unit box packaging.

Process 121 — 포장(박스) (unit box packaging). The camera unit and accessories prepared in process 120 are placed into the UNIT BOX (30201153, qty 1) with PE FOAM bottom pad (30402893, qty 1) and silica gel desiccant (30400105, qty 1). Product label (30101295, qty 1) is attached to the unit box. Box and PE FOAM moulding defects confirmed absent by visual inspection. Accessory completeness confirmed before box closure.

Process 122 — 포장(라벨부착) (label attachment). PE FOAM top pad (30402892, qty 1) is placed over the camera unit inside the unit box. Mount template (30601696, qty 1) is inserted. Label print specification and serial number confirmed by visual inspection. PE FOAM top moulding defects confirmed absent. Performed by WORKER_PACK_LABEL (2 persons).

Process 123 — 포장(카톤박스) (carton box packaging). Unit-box label (30100210, qty 1) is attached and the individually boxed camera units are consolidated into the shipping carton (30201154, NK, qty 0.166 — 1 carton per 6 units). Packaging material completeness and label specification confirmed before carton closure. This step constitutes the final stage of the MODEL_C NVD assembly and packaging sequence.
Sampling rate of OQC process
OQC samping inspection process. Equipment: Computer + Monitor DELL allocated to OQC process.
Dependency type of process OQC. SEQUENCE — ready when any predecessor in DepPrev completed.
Predecessor process codes of OQC. ';'-separated across all camera models — OQC is a shared sampling station that any model can enter after its final pre-pack process.

Successor process codes of OQC. ';'-separated across all camera models — OQC routes to each model's first packaging node. Reverse-edge declaration (avoids modifying per-model MP files when a shared station is added).
Defect rate of OQC sampling — 0 (not a defect-producing step, just an inspection gate).
RMA repair process. Equipment : Soldering iron WS081 allocated entirely to RMA repair process. CT=600s
A collection that classifies all manufacturing process nodes by their dependency type, enabling the PPO agent to select executable processes from the ready queue during simulation.
A collection of references to process nodes whose DepType is SEQUENCE and DepPrev is empty. These processes require only InputBOM stock satisfaction to become ready.
Reference to VD7 input process node. No predecessor required. Ready when InputBOM stock is satisfied.
Reference to BT5 input process node. No predecessor required. Ready when InputBOM stock is satisfied.
Reference to NVD input process node. No predecessor required. Ready when InputBOM stock is satisfied.

A collection of references to process nodes whose DepType is SEQUENCE and DepPrev is not empty. These processes require at least one predecessor process to be completed and InputBOM stock satisfaction to become ready.
Reference to VD7 process node. Predecessor exists. Ready when predecessor completed and InputBOM stock is satisfied.
Reference to BT5 process node. Predecessor exists. Ready when predecessor completed and InputBOM stock is satisfied.
Reference to NVD process node. Predecessor exists. Ready when predecessor completed and InputBOM stock is satisfied.

Reference to OQC shared sampling node. Predecessor is each model's final pre-pack process (DepPrev='VD7_100;BT5_110;NVD_110'). DepType=SEQUENCE — ready when any one predecessor is completed. SamplingRate=0.05 governs probabilistic consumption (5% of units actually inspected, 95% bypass).
A collection of references to process nodes whose DepType is JOIN. Thses processes require all predecessor processes to be completed and InputBOM stock satisfaction to become ready
Reference to VD7 process node. All predecessors required. Ready when all predecessors completed and InputBOM stock is satisfied.
Reference to BT5 process node. All predecessors required. Ready when all predecessors completed and InputBOM stock is satisfied.
Reference to NVD process node. All predecessors required. Ready when all predecessors completed and InputBOM stock is satisfied.

Workstation information for the focus adjustment line in CPRO camera assembly. Covers focus setting steps (VD7_30, NVD_40) across MODEL_A and MODEL_C. Headcount: 3 persons. Work hours: 09:00–18:00, break 60 min.

Workstation information for the semi-assembly line in CPRO camera assembly. Covers semi-assembly steps (VD7_50, VD7_80, VD7_80-1, BT5_40, BT5_41, BT5_42, BT5_60, BT5_61, NVD_50, NVD_51, NVD_60, NVD_61, NVD_80) across MODEL_A, MODEL_B, and MODEL_C. Headcount: 11 persons. Work hours: 09:00–18:00, break 60 min.

Workstation information for the SET assembly line in CPRO camera assembly. Covers SET assembly steps across MODEL_A (VD7_40, VD7_40-1, VD7_50-1, VD7_50-2, VD7_60, VD7_70, VD7_70-1, VD7_70-2, VD7_90), MODEL_B, and MODEL_C. Headcount: 16 persons arranged in subgroups (3, 4, 3, 4, 2). Inspection-dedicated subgroup allocated from within this headcount. Work hours: 09:00–18:00, break 60 min.
Workstation for the inspection process within the SET assembly stage in camera manufacturing

Workstation information for the aging test line in CPRO camera assembly. Covers aging test steps (VD7_100, BT5_100, NVD_110) across MODEL_A, MODEL_B, and MODEL_C. Headcount: 6 persons. Work hours: 09:00–18:00, break 60 min.

Workstation information for the OQC (Outgoing Quality Control) line in CPRO camera assembly. Performs sampling inspection on 5% of finished units across MODEL_A, MODEL_B, and MODEL_C prior to packaging. OQC inspection time: 10 minutes per unit. Headcount: 4 persons arranged in two groups of 2. Work hours: 09:00–18:00, break 60 min.

Workstation information for the packaging line in CPRO camera assembly. Covers all packaging steps (VD7_110, VD7_110-1, VD7_110-2, VD7_110-3) across MODEL_A, MODEL_B, and MODEL_C. Total headcount: 6 persons. Among the 6 workers, 2 persons are dedicated to label attachment (VD7_110-2, BT5_122, NVD_122). Work hours: 09:00–18:00, break 60 min.
A collection of scalar weight values that define the relative importance of each reward component in the PPO agnet's reward function. All weights must sum to 1.0
Weights applied to the time elapsed penalty. Penalizes the agent proportionally to simulation time consumed per episode, encouraging faster completion of production targets.
Weight applied to the energy comsumption penalty. Penalizes the agent for total power consumed across all process nodes per episode, incentivizing energy-efficient scheduling

Weight applied to the stock overflow penalty. Penalizes the agent when inventory of any item exceeds the maximum stock threshold, reflecting excess holding costs and capital inefficiency caused by over-ordering.

Weight applied to the stock shortage penalty. Penalizes the agent when inventory of any item falls below the minimum stock threshold, reflecting the risk of production stoppages caused by insufficient material supply.
Weight applied to the throughout reward. Rewards the agent for each unit of completed production, incentivizing maximization of output within the simulation episode.

Weight applied to the idle worker penalty. Penalizes the agent when any workstation has idle workers exceeding a defined threshold duration, indicating inefficient scheduling and underutilization of available labour capacity.
A collection of fixed simulation parameters that govern warehouse replenishment, SMT line behaviour, work-in-progress control, and reinforcement learning execution for CPRO.
Default parameter collection for solder cream usage and validity management on SMT lines.
Daily solder cream consumption per SMT line in grams. Used with LineCount to calculate total daily solder cream consumption across all lines.
Capacity of a single solder cream container, when cumulative daily usage exceeds this value, a new container is opened.
Shelf life management policy for solder cream after opening.
Key operational parameters and default values for SMT (Surface Mount Technology) line configuration and equipment maintenance in the camera manufacturing simulation model.
Replenishment lead time in hours (Default: 24 hours = 1 day)

The total scheduled break duration per working day at a manufacturing workstation, expressed in minutes. Includes all rest periods such as lunch breaks. Effective working time per day is calculated as the difference between work end time and work start time minus the total break duration.

Threshold duration in seconds beyond which a worker in idle state is considered inefficiently unutilised. If any worker remains idle continuously for longer than this value, the W6_IdleWorker penalty is applied to the agent reward. Set to 300 seconds (5 minutes) as the baseline tolerance for scheduling gaps between process assignments.
Rated Power when process is idle
Collection of dynamic state variables that are initialized at the start of each simulation episode and continuously updated during SimPy discrete event execution.

Flag indicating whether the current production cycle has reached a terminal node in the KnowledgeGraph. Set to True when a ProcessCode with no successor edges is completed, triggering Throughput increment and completed set reset.
Cumulative count of completed production cycles within the current episode. Incremented by 1 each time a terminal node ProcessCode is completed. Episode terminates when Throughput reaches target_qty.

Cumulative electrical energy consumed across all workstations from episode start to current simulation time. Incremented in process_job() by (CycleTimeSec * RatedPowerKw) / 3600 per completed process.
Cumulative count of stock shortage events within the current episode. Incremented each time present_stock falls below MinStock during warehouse consume().
Cumulative count of stock overflow events within the current episode. Incremented each time present_stock exceeds MaxStock during warehouse replenish().
Cumulative count of idle worker violations within the current episode. Incremented when any workstation has idle workers exceeding break and non-working hour.

Maximum possible energy consumption in kWh for a single episode, calculated as the sum of (CycleTimeSec * RatedPowerKw) / 3600 across all GraphNode processes. Used as normalisation denominator for EpisodeEnergyKwh in W2_Energy reward calculation.

Discounted cumulative reward calculated from episode rewards using Gamma (G = reward + Gamma * G, computed in reverse). Used as the target value for the Critic and as the baseline for advantage estimation.

Normalised difference between EpisodeReturns and Critic value predictions, scaled to zero mean and unit standard deviation. Indicates how much better or worse an action was compared to the expected value.
A collection of parameters governing initial stock levels, replenishment triggers, and lot size calculations for the warehouse simulation in CPRO.
Ratio of expected demand quantity used to calculate the replenishment order quantity for RESISTOR components. Order quantity is derived as total demand multiplied by this ratio.
Maximum stock quantity for RESISTOR components up to which inventory is replenished when an order is placed.
Defines the static architecture parameters of the GNN and PPO neural networks used in the reinforcement learning agent. All values are fixed before training and loaded once via path_extractor.py

Specifies Simulation Model.

definition.text: Specifies Simulation Model.
A collection of static configuation properties that govern the execution of the discrete-event reinforcement learning simulation for CPRO
Maximum number of training episodes for the PPO reinforcement learning agent for CPRO. Early termination applies if convergence is detected before this limit.

A collection of process node definitions used to construct the ProcessKnowledgeGraph for CPRO. Each child collection represents a product model variant, containing individual process node sub-collections with feature values serving as GNN input vectors

A collection of process node definitions for MODEL_A(VD7) used as graph nodes in the ProcessKnowledgeGraph for CPRO. Each child collection represents an individual process node carrying the rated power consumption value that is not defined in the ManufacturingProcess Submodel.

Process node representing the firmware input step of MODEL_A (VD7) used as a graph node in the ProcessKnowledgeGraph for CPRO. Rate power is derived from MODULE group compressor allocation proportional to CycleTimeSec

The time required to complete one unit of work at a manufacturing process step, measured in seconds. Used in discrete event simulation to define the duration of a process step timeout. Represents the standard cycle time under normal operating conditions with the assigned worker group and equipment.

The proportion of non-conforming units produced at a manufacturing process step relative to the total number of units processed. Expressed as a dimensionless decimal value. Used in discrete event simulation to determine stochastic defect occurrence per unit processed at each step.

A manufacturing process step in which loaded firmware data is verified for compliance with product specification and buyer requirements. No physical input materials are consumed. Verification is performed using the OEM specification document as the reference standard. Input sequence order must be strictly observed to ensure data integrity.

A manufacturing process step that confirms complete and successful loading of firmware data onto the camera module PCB. Completion of firmware input is verified to be 100% before the assembly advances to the next stage. Firmware compliance with product and buyer specification is re-confirmed against the OEM specification document. Input sequence order must be strictly observed.

A manufacturing process step in which a unique MAC address and model name are programmed into a camera module using an input program interface. MAC address uniqueness must be guaranteed across all units to prevent duplication. Model name is verified via device command output. This step concludes the firmware input process group and the sub-assembly proceeds to the focus adjustment process upon completion.

A manufacturing process step in which a lens holder, actuator, lens, and fastening hardware are assembled onto a sensor board sub-assembly. The lens holder geometry is defined by CNC post-processing specification. Torque requirements for fastening must be measured and confirmed periodically using a torque meter. Absence of foreign matter on the TDN filter must be confirmed visually before the step is considered complete.

displayName.text: SENSOR BOARD Integration onto Main Board (Process 20-1)

definition.text: A manufacturing process step in which a completed sensor board sub-assembly is integrated with the main board PCB using insulation seat and fastening screws. Correct TDN actuator orientation must be confirmed against reference photograph. Absence of foreign matter and connector integrity are verified visually before the step is considered complete. Completed sub-assemblies are transferred to the subsequent assembly line in batches via cart.

A manufacturing process step in which the optical focus of a camera module is adjusted and verified following sensor board sub-assembly integration. A dome cover is used as a reference fixture during visual focus inspection. Lens protrusion length is measured using a vernier caliper to confirm correct focal distance. No physical input materials are consumed at this step.

A manufacturing process step in which a gimbal front housing, infrared PCB, infrared rubber seal, and fastening screws are assembled into a gimbal sub-assembly unit. Correct orientation and seating of the infrared rubber component must be confirmed visually against a reference photograph. This step begins independently upon SMT completion and its output converges with the sensor board sub-assembly at the subsequent JOIN process step.

A manufacturing process step at which the gimbal sub-assembly and the sensor board sub-assembly converge and are integrated into a single unit. Gimbal module bracket and tilt bracket are fastened using tapping screws. IR harness routing direction and optical centre alignment between lens and IR rubber seal must be confirmed visually before the step is considered complete. This step is a JOIN convergence point in the assembly flow.

A manufacturing process step in which the bottom case housing is assembled with a cable rubber grommet, waterproof cable harness, and cable tie. Cable routing and tie securing must be confirmed before the step is considered complete. This step begins independently upon SMT completion and its output converges with the focus adjustment sub-assembly at the subsequent JOIN process step.

A manufacturing process step at which the bottom case sub-assembly and the focus-adjusted camera sub-assembly converge and are integrated. The main board PCB is thermally coupled to the housing via a thermal pad and mechanically fastened using screws. Signal connectivity between the sensor board and main board is established via micro coaxial wire harness. This step is a JOIN convergence point in the assembly flow.

A manufacturing process step in which gimbal support and rotation limit bracket components are installed onto the integrated bottom case sub-assembly to complete the bottom case assembly stage. Gimbal support bracket with sponge pad is fastened using machine screws with controlled torque. Rotation limits bracket orientation must be confirmed against reference to ensure correct mechanical constraint direction. Completed sub-assemblies are transferred to the subsequent assembly line in batches via cart.

description.text: GIMBAL + BOTTOM ASS'Y (Process 60)

definition.text: A manufacturing process step at which the gimbal sub-assembly and the bottom case sub-assembly are mechanically fastened together using cross-head screws. MCX cable connectivity between the sensor board and main board is confirmed for complete insertion and absence of damage. Gimbal directional orientation is verified against reference photograph. This step is a JOIN convergence point receiving outputs from the gimbal assembly and bottom case assembly streams.

A manufacturing process step in which the assembled camera module undergoes the first stage of functional and visual inspection. Inspection is performed by a dedicated sub-group within the SET assembly worker group. Units identified as non-conforming at this step are diverted to the RMA repair process before re-entering the assembly flow.

A manufacturing process step in which the assembled camera module undergoes the second stage of functional and visual inspection following the first inspection stage. Inspection is performed by a dedicated sub-group within the SET assembly worker group. Units identified as non-conforming at this step are diverted to the RMA repair process before re-entering the assembly flow.

A manufacturing process step in which the assembled camera module undergoes the third and final stage of functional and visual inspection. Upon successful completion, the inspected sub-assembly proceeds to the SET assembly JOIN process where it merges with the upper housing sub-assembly. Units identified as non-conforming are diverted to the RMA repair process.

A manufacturing process step in which the upper housing sub-assembly is constructed by integrating the dome cover, bubble gasket, dome stopper, and adhesive vent onto the upper case. All sealing and retention components must be confirmed correctly oriented and free of foreign matter before mechanical fastening. This step begins independently upon SMT completion and its output merges with the inspected camera assembly at the SET assembly JOIN process.

A manufacturing process step in which the main gasket is installed into the upper case housing groove and the upper and lower camera housings are mechanically joined using Torx screws. Correct gasket seating and absence of foreign matter must be confirmed before fastening. This step completes the upper housing sub-assembly which subsequently merges with the inspected camera assembly at the SET assembly JOIN process.

A manufacturing process step at which the inspected camera sub-assembly and the completed upper housing sub-assembly are mechanically joined into a finished camera unit. IR sponge is cleaned and installed to suppress infrared leakage. Dome cover protective film is applied to prevent surface damage during subsequent handling. This step is a JOIN convergence point constituting the final mechanical assembly stage before aging test.

A manufacturing process step in which a fully assembled camera unit is operated continuously for a defined duration to detect latent defects and early-stage failure mechanisms. Units that fail or exhibit anomalous behaviour during the aging period are removed from the production flow and directed to corrective action before shipment.

A manufacturing process step in which all field installation accessories are prepared and packaged alongside the finished camera unit. Accessory items include mounting hardware, a drive tool, antistatic protective bags, and a waterproof connector cap. Completeness of all accessory items must be confirmed by visual inspection before the unit proceeds to the individual box packaging step.

A manufacturing process step in which the finished camera unit is placed into an individual product box together with a PE foam bottom insert for cushioning and a silica gel desiccant for moisture control. Box structural integrity and foam insert moulding quality must be confirmed before the camera unit is placed inside. Accessory completeness is verified before box closure.

A manufacturing process step in which the PE foam top insert is placed over the camera unit inside the individual product box and the product identification label is attached to the box exterior. Label print specification compliance and serial number uniqueness must be confirmed before the box proceeds to carton packaging. Foam insert moulding quality is verified visually at this step.

A manufacturing process step in which the individually boxed camera unit is consolidated into a shipping carton together with a mount template and CD manual. Eight individual unit boxes are packed per carton. Packaging material completeness and label specification compliance must be confirmed before carton closure. This step constitutes the final stage of the camera module manufacturing and packaging sequence.

A collection of process node definitions for MODEL_B(BT5) used as graph nodes in the ProcessKnowledgeGraph for CPRO. Each child collection represents an individual process node carrying the rated power consumption value that is not defined in the ManufacturingProcess Submodel.

A collection of process node definitions for MODEL_C(NVD) used as graph nodes in the ProcessKnowledgeGraph for CPRO. Each child collection represents an individual process node carrying the rated power consumption value that is not defined in the ManufacturingProcess Submodel.

A manufacturing process step in which firmware data is loaded into a camera module printed circuit board and a unique MAC address with model name is programmed via a dedicated jig interface. Jig connection must be made with the power in the OFF state before initiating data transfer. This step is the first in the firmware input sequence and is triggered upon SMT completion.

A manufacturing process step in which firmware data loading on the camera module printed circuit board continues sequentially after the initial firmware input step. No additional physical input materials are consumed. Firmware compliance with product and buyer specification is verified against the OEM specification document.

A manufacturing process step that confirms complete and successful loading of firmware data onto the camera module printed circuit board. Completion of firmware input is verified to be 100% before the assembly advances. Input sequence order must be strictly observed.

A manufacturing process step in which a MAC label is attached to the firmware-loaded printed circuit board to externally indicate the device identifier. Label print specification compliance and serial number uniqueness must be confirmed before the sub-assembly is transferred. This step concludes the firmware input process group.

A manufacturing process step in which an M12 lens is mounted onto the main printed circuit board and fastened with controlled torque to form an optical module sub-assembly. Lens orientation and seating must be confirmed against reference photograph. This step begins independently upon SMT completion and its output proceeds to the focus adjustment process.

A manufacturing process step in which the optical focus of a camera module is adjusted and the lens position is permanently fixed using ultraviolet-cured adhesive. The bonding adhesive is cured under a controlled UV curing unit. Connector integrity and absence of foreign matter must be confirmed before completion. No additional physical input materials are consumed.

A manufacturing process step in which the front housing case is assembled with sealing gaskets, glass windows, and an adhesive vent. Each gasket must be confirmed correctly seated within the case groove. Window components must be installed with the protruding section oriented toward the outer housing surface. This step begins independently upon SMT completion.

A manufacturing process step in which a thermally conductive heat sink stack and the POE/H2IR printed circuit board are installed onto the front housing sub-assembly using a window bracket and machine screws. Thermal pad and adhesive tape orientation must be confirmed before the printed circuit board is mounted. Torque specification must be observed during fastening.

A manufacturing process step at which the focused module sub-assembly converges with the front housing sub-assembly and internal flexible cable harnesses are connected through machined standoff spacers. Connector seating and cable routing must be confirmed before the assembly is transferred. This step is a JOIN convergence point.

displayName.text: Front Assy JOIN with FW PCB (Process 53)

definition.text: A manufacturing process step at which the firmware-loaded printed circuit board sub-assembly is mechanically fastened onto the front housing sub-assembly using cross-head screws. Printed circuit board orientation, screw torque, and connector integrity must be confirmed before transfer. This step is a JOIN convergence point in the front assembly stage.

A manufacturing process step in which the rear housing case is prepared with side cover gasket, cable rubber, and pre-installed mounting screws. Gasket and rubber seating must be confirmed without displacement before fastening. This step begins independently upon SMT completion.

A manufacturing process step in which the waterproof RJ45 and DC jack cable harness is routed through the rear housing together with an O-ring terminal and a pressed cable bracket. Bracket fastening, cable routing direction, and connector integrity must be confirmed before transfer. A wire harness core sleeve is applied to suppress electromagnetic interference.

A manufacturing process step at which the front housing sub-assembly and the rear housing sub-assembly converge and are mechanically joined to form the camera body. A thermal pad is placed at the heater contact interface during convergence to ensure thermal coupling between heater printed circuit board and housing. This step is a JOIN convergence point.

A manufacturing process step in which the bottom case housing is assembled with conduit cap and sealing gaskets to form the bottom housing sub-assembly. Gasket seating and cap orientation must be confirmed before mounting. This step begins independently upon SMT completion.

A manufacturing process step at which the gimbal-completed camera body and the bottom housing sub-assembly converge and are joined together with the top cover. Cover orientation and connector integrity must be confirmed visually. This step is a JOIN convergence point.

A manufacturing process step in which a MAC address label is attached to the assembled housing to externally indicate the device identifier. Label print specification compliance and serial number uniqueness must be confirmed before the assembled unit advances.
A manufacturing process step that completes the SET assembly stage prior to camera test inspection. Specific work content and cycle time pending final standardisation.

A manufacturing process step in which the assembled camera module undergoes the first stage of functional and visual inspection. Inspection is performed by a dedicated sub-group within the SET assembly worker group. Units identified as non-conforming are diverted to the RMA repair process before re-entering the assembly flow.

A manufacturing process step in which the assembled camera module undergoes the second stage of functional and visual inspection following the first inspection stage. Inspection is performed by a dedicated sub-group within the SET assembly worker group. Units identified as non-conforming are diverted to the RMA repair process.

A manufacturing process step in which the assembled camera module undergoes the third and final stage of functional and visual inspection. Upon successful completion, the inspected sub-assembly proceeds to the side cover assembly process. Units identified as non-conforming are diverted to the RMA repair process.

A manufacturing process step in which the lateral housing cover is bonded with an adhesive vent and fastened to the camera body, accompanied by application of protective films and placement of a desiccant inside the housing. Vent attachment, screw torque, and film placement must be confirmed visually before transfer.

A manufacturing process step in which a fully assembled camera unit is operated continuously for a defined duration to detect latent defects and early-stage failure mechanisms. Units that fail or exhibit anomalous behaviour during the aging period are removed from the production flow and directed to corrective action before shipment.

A manufacturing process step in which all field installation accessories are prepared and packaged alongside the finished camera unit. Accessory items typically include mounting hardware, drive tools, antistatic protective bags, and a waterproof connector cap. Completeness of all accessory items must be confirmed by visual inspection before the unit proceeds to the individual box packaging step.

A manufacturing process step in which the finished camera unit is placed into an individual product box together with a PE foam bottom insert for cushioning and a silica gel desiccant for moisture control. A product identification label is attached to the box exterior. Box structural integrity and foam insert moulding quality must be confirmed before the camera unit is placed inside.

A manufacturing process step in which the PE foam top insert is placed over the camera unit inside the individual product box and a mount template is inserted. Label print specification compliance and foam moulding quality must be confirmed by visual inspection.

A manufacturing process step in which the individually boxed camera units are consolidated into a shipping carton together with a unit-box label. Multiple individual unit boxes are packed per carton according to the defined ratio. Packaging material completeness and label specification must be confirmed before carton closure. This step constitutes the final stage of the camera module manufacturing and packaging sequence.

A collection that classifies all manufacturing process nodes by their dependency type for CPRO. Each sub-collection gourps process node references by their ready condition structure, providing the candidate pool from which the PPO agent selects the next process to execute

A collection of references to process nodes whose DepType is SEQUENCE and DepPrev is empty for CPRO. A process node referenced here becomes ready when all items in its InputBOM are sufficiently stocked, with no predecessor completion required.

A collection of references to process nodes whose DepType is SEQUENCE and DepPrev is not empty for CPRO. A process node referenced here becomes ready when at least one predecessor process is completed and all items in its InputBOM are sufficiently stocked.

A collection of references to process nodes whose DepType is JOIN for CPRO. A process node referenced here becomes ready only when all predecessor processes are completed and all items in its InputBOM are sufficiently stocked.

The estimated rated power consumption in kilowatts allocated to a manufacturing process node, derived from the total rated power of shared equipment distributed proportionally by process cycle time ratio within the same provess group.

A collection of scalar weight values that define the relative importance of each reward component in the PPO agent's reward function for CPRO. Weights are fixed hyperparameters set prior to training and applied at every simulation step to compute the weighted sum of reward signals.

A scalar coefficient that scales the time elapsed penalty term in a weighted reward function, controlling the degree to which simulation time consumption is penalized relative to other reward components

A scalar coefficient that scales the time elapsed penalty term in a weighted reward function, controlling the degree to which simulation time consumption is penalized relative to other reward components.

A scalar coefficient that scales the work-in-progress violation penalty term in a weighted reward function, controlling the degree to which exceeding WIP capacity limits is penalized relative to other reward components.
A scalar coefficient that scales the throughput reward term in a weighted reward function, controlling the degree to which production output is rewarded relative to other reward components,

The duration in seconds required for an adhesive or bonding material to fully polymerize and reach its design mechanical strength after application, during which the bonded assembly must remain undisturbed.

displayName.text: NVD1 CPRO향 미니돔 IP 카메라 (NO LOGO)

definition.text: Concept node representing an NVD1-family mini-dome IP camera with 5MP resolution, PoE power delivery, TDN (True Day/Night) mechanical IR-cut filter switching, and high-power infrared LED illumination (H2IR). Acts as the root node of the complete assembly bill-of-materials hierarchy.

A list of references to manufacturing process group assets that a workstation line is assigned to execute. Each reference points to a SubmodelElementCollection defined in the ManufacturingProcess Submodel. Enables simulation and scheduling systems to resolve all process groups associated with a given worker group by traversing this list, and supports multi-model variant assignments where the same worker group executes equivalent process groups across MODEL_A, MODEL_B, and MODEL_C.

A manufacturing workstation designated for firmware programming operations on electronic assemblies. Workers at this station load, verify, and confirm embedded software using USB jig board equipment and assign unique device identifiers. The station is shared across multiple product model variants produced sequentially on the same line.

A manufacturing workstation designated for lens holder and sensor board assembly operations. Workers at this station mount the lens holder, TDN actuator, and associated components onto the sensor board sub-assembly and integrate the completed sensor board onto the main board PCB. The station is shared across multiple product model variants produced sequentially on the same line.

A manufacturing workstation designated for optical focus adjustment operations on camera module sub-assemblies. Workers at this station adjust and verify the focal length of the camera module using dome cover reference fixtures and vernier caliper measurement. The station is shared across applicable product model variants produced sequentially on the same line.

A manufacturing workstation designated for semi-assembly operations in IP camera module production. Workers at this station perform independent sub-assembly processes including bottom case assembly, upper housing assembly, and other preparatory assembly steps that feed into the SET assembly line as JOIN inputs. The station is shared across multiple product model variants produced sequentially on the same line.

A manufacturing workstation designated for SET assembly and inspection operations in IP camera module production. Workers are arranged in fixed seating subgroups of (3, 4, 3, 4, 2) totalling 16 persons. A subset of workers is dynamically allocated to inspection-only duties based on subgroup combinations. The station handles gimbal assembly, combined assembly, inspection, and SET assembly process groups across all applicable product model variants.
Inspection Line for SET Assembly Process

A manufacturing workstation designated for aging test operations in IP camera module production. Workers at this station subject fully assembled camera units to continuous operation for a defined duration to detect latent defects and early-stage failure mechanisms prior to packaging. The station is shared across all applicable product model variants produced sequentially on the same line.

A manufacturing workstation designated for outgoing quality control sampling inspection of finished camera units prior to packaging. A defined percentage of completed units are selected for functional and visual inspection to verify product conformance before shipment. Workers are arranged in two groups of two persons to enable parallel inspection operations.

A manufacturing workstation designated for packaging operations in IP camera module production. Workers at this station package finished camera units with all required accessories, protective materials, and documentation into individual unit boxes and shipping cartons. The station is shared across all applicable product model variants produced sequentially on the same line.

The daily scheduled end time of manufacturing operations at a workstation. Expressed in HH:MM format. Actual end time may extend beyond the scheduled time subject to production volume requirements on a given day.
The daily scheduled start time of manufacturing operations at a workstation. Expressed in HH:MM format. No shift rotation applies; all workers begin at the same time each working day.

The total scheduled break duration per working day at a manufacturing workstation, expressed in minutes. Includes all rest periods such as lunch breaks. Effective working time per day is calculated as the difference between work end time and work start time minus the total break duration.

Scalar weight coefficient applied to the stock overflow penalty component of the PPO agent reward function. Activated when present_stock of any managed item exceeds MaxStock, penalizing excess inventory holding cost and capital inefficiency.

Scalar weight coefficient applied to the idle worker penalty component of the PPO agent reward function. Activated when any workstation records idle worker time exceeding a defined threshold, penalizing inefficient labour scheduling and underutilisation of available workforce capacity.

Maximum tolerated continuous idle duration per worker in seconds before the W6_IdleWorker penalty is triggered in the PPO agent reward function. Default value is 300 s (5 minutes), derived from 6 × 60.
Top-level dollection defining the neural network architecture used in the GNN+PPO reinforcement learning agent for manufacturing process scheduling optimisation.
Graph Neural Network module that encodes process nodes and edges from the Knowledge Graph into embeddings passed to the PPO agent.
Number of numerical features per process node used as GNN input,
Number of neurons in hidden layers of GNN and PPO networks
Dimension of node embedding output from GNN passed to PPO
Number of stacked layers in GNN or PPO network modules.
Proximal Policy Optimisation module receiving GNN embeddings and outputting action selection and value estimation through Actor and Critic subnetworks.
Step size applied during gradient updates of PPO Actor and Critic networks.
PPO clipping parameter that constrains the ratio of new to old policy probability, preventing excessively large policy updates.
Discount factor applied to future rewards in PPO value estimation. Values closer to 1.0 prioritise long-term rewards
Policy network that takes GNN node embeddings as input and outputs a probability distribution over available(ProcessCode, WorkstationId) action pairs.
Generalised Advantage Estimation lambda. Controls bias-variance tradeoff in advantage calculation. Higher values reduce bias but increase variance
Coefficient for entropy bonus added to PPO loss to encourage exploration and prevent premature convergence to suboptimal policies
Coefficient scaling the Critic value loss relative to the Actor policy loss in the combined PPO objective function
Number of experience samples drawn from the rollout buffer per gradient update step
Input demension of Actor network, equal to GNN node embedding output dimension.

Runtime state container for the GNN+PPO agent simulation environment. All variables are reset on env.reset() and mutated exclusively by SimPy process events during episode execution. No variable in this collection holds a fixed value.
Boolean state variable representing single production cycle completion status within one simulation episode.
Integer counter tracking total finished products produced from episode start to current simulation time
Episode-scoped float accumulator for total energy consumption in Kwh. Reset to 0.0 on env.reset(). Used directly as penalty input for W2_Energy reward calculation.
Episode-scoped integer counter for inventory shortage violations. Used as penalty input for W4_StockShortage reward calculation. Reset to 0 on env.reset().
Episode-scoped integer counter for inventory overflow violations. Used as penalty input for W3_StockOverflow reward calculation. Reset to 0 on env.reset().
Episode-scoped integer counter for workforce underutilisation violations. Used as penalty input for W6_IdleWorker reward calculation. Reset to 0 on env.reset().
Episode-scoped float constant set once at initialisation from KnowledgeGraph node data. Does not change during episode.
